title: Tenant islands and guarded admin bridge: RBAC v2 role model proposal
creator: Daniel Park
description: Proposal for RBAC v2 role model focusing on tenant-scoped resource hierarchy, explicit scope derivation, and a guarded admin bridge pattern. Goals: 1) enable least-privilege for cross-tenant operators, 2) support fine-grained permission matrices that map actions to resource classes and scopes, 3) integrate audit logging and SSO/SAML context into authorization decisions, and 4) provide migration path from RBAC v1. The model introduces: - Resource domain tree (Organization > Project > Model > Endpoint) with explicit inheritance rules, - Scope tokens (read, write, manage, admin) attached to role bindings with optional scope-restrictions (timebox, IP, env), - Admin bridge role: a constrained cross-tenant elevation that requires breakglass flow, explicit justification, and time-limited session. This ticket captures design, trade-offs, API contract examples, audit-event schema, and SSO/SAML mapping guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Security and Platform leads
Permission matrix for core resource types (Org/Project/Model/Endpoint) defined and exampled
RBAC API surface (grant/revoke/evaluate) proto defined with SSO/SAML context fields
Audit event schema defined and sample logs for allow/deny/elevation events provided
Migration runbook drafted for RBAC v1 -> v2 with validation checks
decision_log: Choose explicit scope derivation over implicit inheritance for write/delete actions to reduce accidental privilege escalation
Guarded admin bridge implemented as a composable role that combines 'admin' capability with temporal constraints and breakglass approval to avoid permanent cross-tenant admin accounts
Include SAML attributes (eduPersonScopedAffiliation, groups) mapping to role templates; do not couple authorization to IdP-specific claims to preserve portability
Audit logging must include immutable context: principal id, role bindings at time-of-decision, SSO session id, SAML assertion id (when available), and justification for elevation events
tradeoffs_and_risks: Explicit scopes increase complexity of role creation and UI; mitigated by role templates and sensible defaults
Temporal elevation (admin bridge) requires robust session revocation; initially implemented with short TTLs and explicit session teardown APIs
Mapping SAML groups to roles may create drift if IdP group membership changes rapidly; mitigation: cache TTL + revalidation hooks and webhook support
Migration can surface leaked broad grants from v1; mitigation: provide audit reports and auto-suggest least-privilege replacements
audit_schema_sample: {timestamp, event_id, principal_id, principal_roles_snapshot, action, resource, decision, reason, sso_session_id, saml_assertion_id, request_id}
Elevation events must include justification and approver_id fields
migration_notes: Step 1: Export v1 grants and map to v2 role templates using heuristics (owner->org-admin, admin->admin-bridge candidate)
Step 2: Run simulation mode where evaluate API returns both v1 and v2 decisions for a subset of traffic and report diffs
Step 3: Gradually flip evaluation path per tenant with telemetry to detect regressions
Step 4: Provide remediation PRs and suggested binding adjustments to tenant admins
